summary: Reviewed the new persisted AI specialist analyses, consolidated Weekly review page, current roadmap and feature tasks. Generated reports are saved per week, but the analysis read endpoint resolves only the current week; Completed weeks currently reads separate Sunday summaries. One focused proposal makes older saved specialist reports accessible without regeneration. Existing adaptation, progression and data-quality plans were excluded. This was a source/documentation review; no application tests or private records were accessed.

ideas.title: One trustworthy check before shipping
ideas.problem: Frontend behavior tests exist without an npm test command. The backend test command depends on a local dependency folder and mixed import roots. Some tests also use dates that age out of the period they query.
ideas.proposal: Create a documented project check command that runs frontend behavior tests, the frontend build, and backend tests in a reproducible environment. Repair confirmed fixture and clock assumptions without weakening behavior assertions.
ideas.benefit: Make every new feature faster to verify and catch regressions before they reach your training workflow.
acceptance_criteria: One documented command runs the relevant frontend and backend checks from a fresh dependency environment.
Tests do not fail merely because today's date changes.
Strength comparison fixtures include the schema the production code needs.
Existing failing assertions are investigated; no tests are deleted or weakened to obtain a passing run.

ideas.title: Pick up where you left off in Data & Sync
ideas.problem: The selected source on Data & Sync is kept only in component state. Opening a link or refreshing returns to Strava even when you were reviewing another source.
ideas.proposal: Keep the active source in a validated URL query parameter. Preserve it across refresh and browser navigation, and make direct links to Apple Health, HealthFit, and Fitbod work.
ideas.benefit: Return directly to the import source you were working on and share precise troubleshooting links.
acceptance_criteria: A direct URL can select any of the four existing source panels.
Refresh and browser Back/Forward restore the selected source.
Unknown source values fall back safely to Strava.
Switching panels never starts an import.

ideas.title: A smoother dashboard without a mouse
ideas.problem: The app shell provides a main landmark, while Data & Sync nests another main inside it. Repeated navigation and unclear landmark structure add friction for keyboard and screen-reader users.
ideas.proposal: Audit the app shell and page wrappers for a single main landmark, add a visible-on-focus skip-to-content link, and check focus placement after route changes. Keep the current visual design.
ideas.benefit: Make the dashboard easier to navigate with a keyboard and clearer for assistive technology.
acceptance_criteria: Each route exposes exactly one main landmark.
The first keyboard shortcut target is a usable skip-to-content link.
Visible focus remains clear on desktop and mobile layouts.
A browser smoke check covers keyboard navigation on Dashboard and Data & Sync.

ideas.title: Keep unfinished set entries when you switch away
ideas.problem: The live strength runner stores reps and weight in component state until Log set succeeds. syncInputs replaces those inputs from saved or target values when the current set changes or the session reloads, so an unfinished entry can disappear after switching exercises or refreshing. Completed-set persistence does not cover this draft state.
ideas.proposal: Keep a small local draft keyed by workout and set ID for unsubmitted reps and weight. Restore it when returning to the same active set, clearly label it as not logged, and offer an explicit discard action. Reconcile drafts with the latest server state before restoring so another tab or a completed workout cannot silently be overwritten. Keep the existing Log set action as the only completion step.
ideas.benefit: Avoid retyping or forgetting the reps and load you just entered when you check another exercise or accidentally refresh mid-workout.
evidence: frontend/src/views/StrengthWorkoutSession.vue: syncInputs and currentSet watcher replace unsaved input values
frontend/src/views/StrengthWorkoutSession.vue: changePosition calls syncInputs after changing the current exercise/set
frontend/src/views/StrengthWorkoutSession.vue: completeCurrentSet persists values only through the explicit completion API
frontend/src/views/StrengthWorkoutSession.vue: onMounted loads saved session state; localStorage usage currently concerns rest sound
docs/sprints/sprint-36-first-party-strength-workout-tracking.md: durable completed sets and live session runner
acceptance_criteria: Editing reps or weight, switching to another set, and returning restores the unfinished values for the original set without changing the other set.
Reloading the same active workout restores the draft with a clear Not logged label; no completion request is sent automatically.
Successful logging or explicit discard clears that set draft; failed logging preserves it for retry.
Completed, abandoned, deleted, or server-updated sets do not silently receive stale draft values; conflicts offer an explicit review or discard choice.
Unavailable browser storage does not prevent logging; explain that draft recovery is unavailable. Tests use synthetic workout data and cover navigation, reload, failed saves, and stale drafts.

ideas.title: Reopen last week’s specialist advice
ideas.problem: AI team reports are saved under a week-specific settings key, but get_analysis always derives the current week. The Completed weeks view renders SundayReview, which reads the separate weekly-review history. Once the calendar advances, the inspected UI has no way to reopen an older saved specialist report and its HEAD COACH synthesis, even though that report remains stored.
ideas.proposal: Extend Completed weeks with a clearly labeled list of saved specialist analyses alongside existing Sunday summaries. Add bounded read-only list and week-detail endpoints and a shareable selected-week URL. Render the original stored report with its generation time and through-date; do not regenerate it or combine it with present-day recovery context. For older reports without saved citation labels, show honest unavailable-evidence states rather than inventing historical context.
ideas.benefit: Revisit the advice and tradeoffs you were given before deciding whether a training change helped, without spending another AI run.
evidence: backend/app/services/team_analysis.py: read_saved_analysis and save_analysis use team_analysis:{week} keys; get_analysis derives only the current week
backend/app/routers/coaching.py: GET /coaching/team-analysis exposes no historical week parameter or listing
docs/specs/001-hybrid-coaching-team/plan.md: per-week AI persistence and separate completed Sunday history
acceptance_criteria: With synthetic saved analyses for two weeks, both appear in a bounded history list and each can be reopened through a selected-week URL.
Opening a historical report uses its saved specialist text, HEAD COACH synthesis, generation timestamp and through-date, with no AI request or plan write.
Sunday summaries remain available and are clearly distinguished from specialist analyses, including weeks with only one report type.
Missing or deleted supporting activities are labeled unavailable; current recovery or profile data is never silently inserted into historical advice.
Invalid weeks, missing reports, empty history and API failures have clear states; tests cover Monday rollover and verify stored reports remain unchanged.
